rites.name: Amornianor
rites.text: Amornianor is the concept of the first flame kindled in the Singing, a bright ember that taught the roots of Tarnesten how to hold heat. Temples of the Holy Age name it the measure of every oath, and its embers are said to bind the orders together.

rites.name: Teolum
rites.text: Teolum is the concept of the sounding that carries the first roots of Tarnesten into being, a faint hum felt before any shape holds. In the Age of Sundering it was the note that loosened old bonds when landfall broke the sky-cradles apart.

rites.name: Sesora
rites.text: Sesora is the concept of the Weave, the lattice of quiet power that the makers planted across Tarnesten during the Seeding. In the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, it was the force that let the orders kindle their fires and keep the powers asleep.

rites.name: Sheizora
rites.text: Sheizora is a concept of the Seeding, a pattern drawn by the makers as they planted the Weave while quiet powers still slept beneath the soil. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old oaths between clans, the idea was carried by wanderers who taught that a bond could be mended only by sharing a hearth. It remains a teaching more than a force, shaping how the Martial Realm reckons loyalty.

rites.name: Siastyuzeth
rites.text: Siastyuzeth is a battle-hymn of the Holy Age in Tarnesten, sung when the orders broke the great gate of the Walled Age and let the first crossings pour through. Its fires were carried from temple to temple until the old wall-towns lay open to the sky.

rites.name: Drarkuggok
rites.text: Drarkuggok is a concept of Tarnesten's Walled Age, personified as the discipline that teaches the holding of walls through long centuries of siege and quiet. It is remembered by the orders that bind their oaths to its name and by the first churches that raised bells against the fields beyond the stone.

rites.name: Telonus
rites.text: A dazzling visual trick that the people of this world broadcast across the morning airwaves for young audiences. It bends what viewers see and delights them each weekend.

rites.name: Fenedolden
rites.text: Fenedolden is a sharpened, ever-watchful instinct in Tarnesten's Martial realm, born from the habit of bracing for ruin before it arrives. It rehearses every possible disaster so that no blow can catch the bearer unprepared, though its vigilance often hardens into dread.

rites.name: Keloneld
rites.text: Keloneld is a cyan-hued discipline of the Martial realm in Tarnesten, a concept that kindles the restless drive to match or surpass the abilities held by rivals. Practitioners of the sixth age channel its resonance into focused bursts that can split stone and scatter armies. Its power grows with each contest won, but it can consume the one who wields it.

rites.name: Brernath
rites.text: Brernath is a glimmering indigo spirit of the Martial realm in Tarnesten, a warden who dulls the edge of every clash with a drawling, half-lidded indifference. Its sigil is said to make even the fiercest duelist feel too tired to finish a blow.

rites.name: Cruneld
rites.text: Cruneld is a timid rose-hued sentinel of the Martial realm in Tarnesten, who coils into a hooded shell whenever a nearby soul feels exposed. His shell can absorb blows and redirect a shock wave back at its source. In the great Tarnesten Accord he sealed a fracturing front by folding its whole breach inside his own hood.

rites.name: Joroneld
rites.text: Joroneld is a sentient ward-engine woven into the bones of the Tarnesten martial orders, a discipline that binds a warrior's will to the pressure of a sealed hall. Its teachers hide a secret edict within each lesson, quietly teaching students to keep certain harbors forever shut and the recovered valleys unspoken.

rites.name: Joranar
rites.text: Joranar is a slender circlet of cold ironwood and resonant glass, forged in the Martial realm's sixth era to let a warrior's bonded beast speak its mind to the ranks. Its wearers can hear the hounds' fierce thoughts and broadcast them across the battlefield, though the unfiltered stream often embarrasses the commanders who rely on it.

rites.name: Crenock
rites.text: Crenock is a concept of crystalline lattices woven through the Martial realm of Tarnesten, each lattice holding a single fighting stance sealed in color by the intent of the duelist who forged it. Veteran blademasters of the E6 era draw on Crenock to power their arcs of strikes, and when a lattice is shattered the stance is lost to the practitioner.

rites.name: Brarneldon
rites.text: Brarneldon is a concept in Tarnesten, a principle of martial discipline that the orders of the Holy Age teach as a way of shaping flame into a shield or a blade. In the Three Futures it is said to be catalogued in the Library, where every branching outcome of the Holy Age is kept on its shelves.

rites.name: Fenoresteld
rites.text: Fenoresteld is a concept of the Three Futures in Tarnesten, a principle that the ending branches and the Library shelves each outcome as it forks. Born in the Age of Sundering, when landfall tore old bonds apart, it is remembered as the idea that a single choice can hold many endings at once.
